Symbol dictionary

How the translator works and where the keys come from

Local contrast separates dark strokes from the background. Column projection separates glyphs; wide groups are split by comparing candidate shapes. Normalized glyphs are matched against image templates. There is no cloud upload, API key, language model, or wallet interaction.

The English alphabet has 26 chart-derived entries plus examples from the supplied image. Russian entries are derived from published readings of this specific image, checked for repeated shapes. This is a partial custom Cyrillic alphabet, not an official Russian Gravity Falls key. Missing letters and the final right-edge symbol remain unresolved.

Spacing is preserved as separators or image gaps. Russian translation uses exact phrase matches and a small word dictionary; unseen sentences remain literal word glosses. Results are not forced to match the expected text.

ALTERNATIVE INTERPRETATION / RUNIC CALENDAR

Runic-calendar lab

Test the image shapes against calendar runes. A visual resemblance is a candidate, not a verified rune assignment. Unknown symbols keep their positions.

Reference runes are loading.

No calendar interpretation has been established. This lab tests shape coverage and keeps unmatched glyphs visible; it does not infer a hidden date from a partial number string.

Review or enter a rune transcription

Click a result row to inspect its symbol candidates. Edit only when the image supports the choice. Typing a rune is a user assignment, not confirmation of its identity.

Historical keys and limits

The first seven Younger Futhark runes form a repeating weekday row. This lab reports the conventional cycle labels A–G, not fixed weekday names: a year and calendar alignment are required.

The golden-number row uses the sixteen Younger Futhark signs plus Arlaug (17), Tvimadur (18), and Belgthor (19). The l/m order variant is exposed because historical rune rows can differ at positions 14–15. Elder Futhark transliteration is a separate comparison, not a calendar-number system. Ingwaz ᛜ/ᛝ therefore has no value in the 19-symbol calendar key.

Automatic candidates use glyph templates rendered with Noto Sans Runic. Only explicitly enumerated long-branch and short-twig variants are included. Source samples use reviewed pixel boundaries shared across methods, so methods cannot change the character count to improve their coverage. Results do not reuse the Russian letters as rune assignments.

Recorded sensitivity audit · 360 comparisons

Six crops were tested in four whole-line orientations and at three score/lead settings, using five interpretations. This is a bounded shape experiment. Low thresholds can assign numbers to non-runic shapes; full coverage alone is not a decipherment.

Date checks

Modern Gregorian checks for the dates visible in the artwork. These are independent of the image interpretation and cannot turn unmatched symbols into a date.

Controls and reproducibility

Controls verify symbol lookup, rejected lookalikes, retained unknown positions, date arithmetic and the reference-font image recognizer. They do not establish recognition accuracy on ancient carvings or prove that this artwork encodes a calendar.

Works offline as a standalone HTML file. Uploaded images and added templates stay in this tab; use Export to save results. Controls and corrections never alter the source image.
